t: I need to touch it to buy it! How haptic information influences consumer shopping behavior across channels - ScienceDirect
s: April 24, 2021 - Consumers manage complex emotional experiences from the marketplace that either drive them towards or deter them from online or offline shopping, given the distinct nature of the two different platforms (Penz and Hogg, 2011). For example, online shopping offers price advantages but lacks a sense of experience; thus, consumers who prefer physical touch will tend to use offline over online platforms (De Canio and Fuentes-Blasco, 2021).

t: What we touch while shopping affects what we buy, researchers say - Big Think
s: April 19, 2022 - Whether it’s running your fingers over fabrics or weighing a coffee mug in your hand, touching a product ensures future recognition of it, according to a 2015 study published in Applied Cognitive Psychology. For instance, those who want to purchase a candy bar are more likely to buy a KitKat over a Snickers, if they’re holding their smartphone in their hand.
